c.tagline: A glamorous Tyrrhenian island of cliffside villas, the luminous Blue Grotto, and iconic sea-stack Faraglioni

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small boutiques and boat operators

taxi.fare: Metered, but often high fixed rates in peak season
taxi.fareNote: Capri's small, winding roads mean taxis are open-top convertibles; fares are notably higher than mainland Italy

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Capri Town and Anacapri are each walkable, but hilly with many stairs; getting between the two towns is by funicular, bus, or taxi

safety.safety: Very safe island, extremely crowded with day-trippers in peak season
safety.crime: Petty theft in crowded areas during peak season is the main concern

hood_landmark.Capri Town (Piazzetta): The Piazzetta (Piazza Umberto I), Capri's famous small square
hood_landmark.Marina Grande: Marina Grande, the island's main harbor
hood_landmark.Anacapri: Villa San Michele and the Monte Solaro chairlift
hood_landmark.Marina Piccola: Marina Piccola's swimming cove beneath the Faraglioni
hood_landmark.Via Krupp / Gardens of Augustus: The Gardens of Augustus and the switchback Via Krupp path

avoid.reason: Nothing dangerous — just overpriced taxis, restaurants and boat tours; confirm prices before committing.

hood_desc: The elegant hilltop town centered on its famous small square, packed with designer boutiques, cafes, and the best people-watching on the island.
The main harbor where ferries and boats arrive, connected to Capri Town by funicular; less glamorous but the practical entry point.
The quieter, higher western town, with Villa San Michele and access to Monte Solaro's panoramic chairlift.
A small pebble cove below the Gardens of Augustus, popular for swimming with views of the Faraglioni sea stacks.
A terraced garden and switchback path offering some of the island's best photo viewpoints over the sea and cliffs.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though many order bottled at restaurants.

transit.sys: Funicular between Marina Grande and Capri Town, plus local bus routes to Anacapri and Marina Piccola
transit.pay: Single tickets or a combined day pass, sold at kiosks
transit.note: Private cars are largely restricted on the island; the funicular, buses, and taxis handle most transport

transport.air: Naples International Airport (NAP), then a ferry from Naples or Sorrento
transport.train: Circumvesuviana train to Sorrento connects with the ferry to Capri
transport.bus: Local buses connect Capri Town, Anacapri, and Marina Piccola
transport.ferry: Frequent ferries and hydrofoils from Naples, Sorrento, and Positano
transport.car: Not practical for visitors; the island is largely car-free for tourists

airport.name: Naples International Airport (via ferry)
airport.distance: ~40 km to Naples port, then a 45-80 min ferry crossing
airport.transport: Taxi/train to Naples or Sorrento port, then ferry to Capri

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A TIM, Vodafone, or WindTre tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for boat and tour guides
tip.r: A cover charge (coperto) is common instead of tipping; rounding up is a nice gesture
